title: The Retriever Should Remember: Experience-Amortized Reranking for Long-Term Agent Memory

visual_explainer.question: Can a memory retriever retain relevance judgments across queries instead of paying to reacquire every score?
visual_explainer.takeaway: EARM stores sparse query-memory relevance scores, completes the causal matrix, and spends new LLM scoring calls only on selected anchors before mixing observed and imputed rankings.
visual_explainer.compared_with: Stateless full pointwise reranking and semantic retrieval over the same fixed Mem0 store and 200-candidate pool.

analysis.tldr: EARM retains sparse query-memory relevance judgments and imputes unscored candidates, reducing direct reranker calls by 74.43% while recovering part of full-reranking accuracy on LoCoMo. The cleanest ablation adds matrix completion to the same observed anchors for +0.78 to +2.79 points. Evidence comes from one fixed memory store and ordered query stream, with incomplete token/latency accounting.
analysis.problem: Long-term memory rerankers repeatedly pay an LLM to score similar memory candidates even when past queries have already revealed reusable relevance structure.
analysis.core_idea: Persist a causal query-memory score matrix, directly score a shrinking mixture of exploitation and exploration anchors, warm-start low-rank completion, and combine observed with imputed scores for top-k context selection.
analysis.agent_loop: query → retrieve fixed candidate pool → score selected anchors → update persistent relevance matrix → complete unobserved scores → select answer context
analysis.retrieval_design: All reported experiments keep the Mem0 store and 200-candidate semantic pool fixed. The mixed-versus-observed-only ablation isolates imputation; proposed scoring outside the first-stage pool is not tested.
compared_to: multiple matrix ranks and top-k sizes
analysis.evidence: LoCoMo top-10 accuracy is 82.21% semantic, 88.83% EARM-r8, and 91.62% full reranking. Completion adds 0.78–2.79 points beyond observed anchors, while direct calls fall from 307,982 to 78,736.
analysis.why_it_matters: It treats retrieval judgments themselves as persistent state and frames reuse versus reacquisition as an amortization decision.
limitations: Only LoCoMo is evaluated, without confidence intervals or significance tests.
The full memory store is built before evaluation and never changes; ingestion, eviction, identity drift, and content updates are absent.
Gains depend on ordered within-conversation low-rank reuse and may disappear for heterogeneous query streams.
Call counts omit tokens, latency, matrix compute, answer calls, ingestion, and dollars.
The budget schedule is fixed by query index, and candidate expansion beyond the semantic pool is proposed but not evaluated.
